items.text: the Form is now as many movements as you like, laid out like the index: drag the grip to re-order, the crossed eye mutes (skips) a movement, S solos it and loops it so you can practise, fold or pin as you wish
each movement has its own length, what the players do, composer's notes, and can hold a look (grid, lines, sounds, mix, tempo) that comes in when it begins
copy or cut a movement, or the whole form, as text; paste it back or into another Battanboo; save a form as a template in "My forms", with Undo for changes
while an overlay covers the grid, the edit tools and the halo, colour and shape bar dim, since you cannot see what they would change

the right-hand rail has a new order. The pencil is on top with its editing tools beneath it, then the clock and the colour/view button, and the heads-up display (mixer, sliders, gestures) is now the bottom button on the right. It stays put whether you play or edit.
held sideways (an iPad or a computer), the whole bar is on one line again; the two-row bar with tempo first is for upright screens
the tempo bar and undo/redo are the first row under the grid; the robot, dice, scenes and recording come second, on upright screens
on an iPad held upright, the tempo and A/B bar has a row of its own, full width, so it can be slid; side by side only on screens 1280 px wide or more
the A and B buttons are round
Battanboo remembers where you left off: the grid, lines, tempo, scale, mix and sound choices come back after a reload or if the page stops (Start blank, in Past, begins empty)
when a newer version is out, a small notice says so and lists what changed; Update opens it, and the next visit says which version you are on
more rhythms: Cumbia, Polka, Tango, Son montuno, Choro, Zouk, Agbekor bell and Afrobeat (simplified sketches)
a form clock in the frame that counts the piece's sections and pulses at each change, with names and notes you can write
a row or column switch now toggles muted and available; always on is a press and hold, so the loudest choice is never an accident
the grid no longer grows slightly on the first touch
